drivers: MW billing rent versus the amended schedule (Black Pearl phases; Barber Lake Halls 1 to 5 from 4Q26 to 1Q27; Stingray 1H27), and any rent credits
Build cost and change orders: Barber Lake EAC ($2,941mn to $2,966mn against a $2,157mn budget; Cipher bears the first $359.3mn), plus Black Pearl and Stingray cost to complete
Tenant and backstop credit: Google backstop for Fluidstack, the AI lab's 10-year extension, and investment-grade hyperscalers at Black Pearl and Stingray
Parent funding and dilution: about $2.16bn of 0% converts (puts October 2029 and November 2030), physical settlement default, the 40.7mn-share exchange, and equity needs for new projects
New leases on the pipeline (Odessa, Reveille, Ulysses; Colchis 1 GW in ERCOT Batch Zero) and the cost of project debt
model:
Economic engine: Cipher builds Texas data center campuses and leases them for 10 to 20 years to hyperscalers and AI tenants, who bring their own GPUs. Each campus is financed with secured high-yield project notes sized against the lease, and parent equity comes from converts (FY25 10-K; 2Q26 10-Q; October 2026 deck).
Revenue map: rent = delivered critical IT MW x contracted $/kW-month x 12, starting hall by hall, plus tenant-paid change orders recognized over the term. Contracted: Barber Lake 300 MW gross (Fluidstack, Google backstop; 20 years after the September 2026 amendment, over $9bn, phased delivery 4Q26 to 1Q27), Black Pearl about 300 MW gross (investment-grade hyperscaler, 15 years, first capacity August 2026), Stingray (investment-grade hyperscaler, 15 years, delivery 1H27). Total 700 gross MW, $16.6bn contracted revenue, 17.3-year WALT, about $843mn average annualized NOI (30 September 2026). Legacy bitcoin mining at Odessa (207 MW, fixed-price Luminant PPA): $24.8mn of revenue in 2Q26.
Cost structure: project operating costs (power, O&M) deducted to reach NOI; corporate compensation ($42.4mn in 2Q26, of which $30.5mn share-based) and G&A; depreciation (mining equipment over about 3 years; data halls once in service); interest ($66.7mn in 2Q26), partly offset by interest income on restricted construction cash ($35.9mn).
Capital and funding: secured project notes, non-recourse except for parent completion guarantees: Cipher Compute 7.125% due 2030 $1,733mn (Ba3/BB-, amortizing with the Google backstop), Black Pearl Compute 6.125% due 2031 $2,000mn, Stingray Compute 6.000% due 2031 $810mn (both Ba2/BB-). Parent: 0% converts due 2031 $1,300mn (conversion price $16.03, put October 2029), 0% converts due 2032 $850mn (conversion price $15.31, put November 2030, issued October 2026), a $200mn revolver (undrawn at 30 June) and a warrant liability of $632.1mn at 30 June (Google warrants over 24.2mn shares at $0.01, issued for the Barber Lake backstop). Barber Lake: EAC $2,941mn to $2,966mn against a $2,157mn budget, with about $750mn more parent equity.
Sensitivities: delivery timing (rent starts only on delivery; rent credits for missed milestones), build cost and change orders (Cipher bears the first $359.3mn at Barber Lake), tenant and backstop credit, high-yield spreads at refinancing, share price (converts, dilution), ERCOT interconnection batch timing, bitcoin price for the residual mining business.
Competitive position: about 3.4 GW of near-term grid pipeline (Colchis 1 GW, McLennan and Mikeska 500 MW each, Ulysses 200 MW, Reveille 70 MW, Apollo up to 900 MW) plus about 2.5 GW of behind-the-meter potential via gas laterals; in-house power origination, engineering and construction; competes with TeraWulf, Applied Digital, IREN, Core Scientific, Galaxy and Hut 8 for hyperscaler leases.
What would break the model: (1) repeated delivery slips that trigger rent credits or tenant termination rights; (2) cost overruns that turn equity returns negative; (3) loss or limitation of the Google backstop or the AI lab extension; (4) a parent funding gap at the 2029 and 2030 convert puts if the stock stays far below the conversion prices; (5) failure to sign new leases on the pipeline before the ERCOT batch and the Odessa power contract (to July 2027) run out.
